# Mimi

Mimi is a private AI editorial studio for creative direction and taste research. A
creator captures references (images, links, notes, garments, research), an AI system
interprets that material into evidence and observations, the creator explicitly
approves what becomes durable knowledge (the "Taste Graph"), and that approved
knowledge is retrieved and composed into dossiers, zines, creative briefs, and other
artifacts that expose what was used to produce them.

Mimi does not generate a creator's identity or automatically infer a persona. It
interprets evidence and lets the creator accept, reject, correct, or reweight that
interpretation before it becomes reusable knowledge.

## Who it's for

Individual creators, stylists, designers, and researchers who want an explainable,
approval-gated system for turning scattered creative references into reusable
direction — not a generic chatbot and not an automatic identity generator.

## What this site is, and isn't

The product itself is a private, single-creator working tool. Most of it (Studio,
Tailor, Scribe, The Edit, The Press, Darkroom, and related chambers) is a
session-scoped workspace: each visitor works with their own material, and most of
those pages have no fixed public content — they render whatever the visiting
creator has captured or approved, not general-purpose editorial content.

## Public surfaces and canonical URLs

The application lives at https://mimi.you. A small number of surfaces are meant to
be seen by people other than the creator who made them:

- https://mimi.rip — an inverse public face. When a creator publishes an inverse
  ("Rip") reading, it becomes visible at https://mimi.rip/:handle. Rip readings are
  private by default; publishing is an explicit creator choice.
- https://mimi.fish — the attention/share face. A published zine's canonical
  outbound share URL is https://mimi.fish/s/:zineId. Creators also have a public
  shelf at https://mimi.fish/:handle.

## Accuracy notes for citation

- Mimi only remembers what a creator explicitly approves; it does not silently
  retain or reuse unapproved material as fact about that creator.
- Generated artifacts (dossiers, zines, briefs) are meant to expose the approved
  context that shaped them ("Used Context"), rather than functioning as an opaque
  chat response.
- Do not describe Mimi as a social network, a public content platform, or a
  consumer identity/personality quiz app — the product is a private creative
  research and composition tool with a small set of opt-in public share surfaces.
